solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Still holding a strike, fanatic borders on expanding growth in Africa

indicators.note: a word that holds something keeps it inside, so the opening word wraps around what follows

parts.note: still water or weather is calm
taken as written
to strike someone is to bash them
a fanatic is a nut, as in 'a fitness nut'

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its outermost letters are wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sculptor's growing obsession, perhaps: a still figure frozen mid-blow, edged by an ever-wider fanatic fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' and 'strike' read as a scene of violence, but they are synonyms for wordplay. CALABASH NUTMEG is a West African tree whose aromatic seeds are used like nutmeg.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree grows wild in tropical West Africa, so describing it as an African plant is a plain botanical description.

clue.text: Russian girl dividing gold stamps found in diner's cupboard down under

indicators.note: something dividing a word splits it apart by sitting in the middle of it
what is found in a place sits within it, so these pieces go inside the next word

parts.note: a diner is a cheap café; the 's reads as 'is'
OR is gold in heraldry
dies are tools that stamp shapes into metal
a typical Russian girl's name

explanation.surface: A Russian girl is sorting a gold stamp collection she discovered in an Australian diner's cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold is heraldic. A COOLGARDIE SAFE is a wet-hessian evaporative cooling cupboard named after the Western Australian goldfields town of Coolgardie.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a wooden frame hung with damp cloth that kept food cool in outback Australia, hence a cupboard from 'down under'.

clue.text: Downs raised weapon in SE Asian republic

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: the landlocked country between Thailand and Vietnam

indicators.note: in a down entry, something raised reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: Troops in a South-East Asian republic hoist their weapons as they move across open downland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downs' suggests rolling English hills, but it is the plural of fine body hair. LANUGO is the soft downy hair covering a foetus.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanugo is a fine, soft growth of hair on newborns and foetuses, which is down in the feathery sense, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Radical Lefty gutted about supporting raised VAT

indicators.note: in a down entry, something raised reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a vat is a large tub

indicators.note: turned about means turned round to face the other way
a gutted thing has had its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A radical left-winger is gutted to be backing a rise in value added tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' and 'Lefty' paint politics, but the radical is chemical. In a down clue 'supporting' places the second piece beneath the first. VAT is Britain's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as one unit; this four-carbon group is a standard example.

clue.text: Seal clasp below notice

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed below another comes after it in the reading

parts.note: to notice something is to see it
a clasp is a fastening catch

explanation.surface: A wax seal and a metal clasp sit beneath an official notice on a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' reads as a stamp on a document, but it is the animal. A SEECATCH is an adult male fur seal of the North Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the name for a mature bull fur seal guarding a breeding territory, a particular kind of the animal.

clue.text: Short fat naked gent stands before iron fist of Will

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its final letter
one piece placed before another comes first in the reading
in a down entry, a thing that stands up reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the word with its last letter dropped

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, a word keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: the two inner letters of the word
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A short, fat man stands stripped bare in front of a bully with an iron fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is Shakespeare: NEAFFE (or neaf) is his word for a fist, as in Henry IV's 'Sweet knight, I kiss thy neaf'. 'Stands' turns both earlier pieces upwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic northern word for the hand clenched tight, used by Shakespeare, so it is a fist as Will would write it.

clue.text: Tense dispute ignoring English film expert in Aramaic?

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
to dispute a point is to argue it
E is the abbreviation for English
a film of moisture is a mist

explanation.surface: A tense row breaks out, leaving out the English-speaking film buff among scholars of ancient languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' points at cinema but means a thin haze. The Targums are Aramaic translations and paraphrases of the Hebrew Bible; a TARGUMIST wrote or studies them.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a scholar works on Aramaic renderings of scripture, so 'expert in Aramaic' is fair, with the question mark admitting it is a narrower specialism.

clue.text: European climbs high East Indian trees

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A European tourist scales the tall trees of the East Indies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like it describes how far the European climbs, but it is the anagram signal. The EMBLIC is the Indian gooseberry tree, Phyllanthus emblica.
explanation.definitionFit: The emblic, or myrobalan, is a tree native to India and South-East Asia, so it is an East Indian tree by botanical range.

clue.text: Edict in favour of papal ambassador that's somehow meant to be included

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: a thing included is taken inside, so these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: a nuncio is the Pope's envoy to a foreign state

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the order of the letters is not fixed

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A decree in favour of the Pope's envoy that was, in some fashion, intended to be inserted into a treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters of 'meant' go inside the envoy's title, after PRO. A PRONUNCIAMENTO is a manifesto or proclamation, especially one issued by Spanish or Latin American insurgents.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a formal public proclamation or decree, from the Spanish, so it serves as a synonym for an official edict.

clue.text: Plant Coliseum-based performers in second entrance to arena

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: every second day is every other day
English National Opera is based at the London Coliseum

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is where you first come in, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A company of Coliseum performers is planted at the arena's second entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coliseum' suggests Rome, but it is the London theatre that is home to English National Opera. OENOTHERA is the evening primrose genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening primrose belongs to this botanical genus, so the Latin genus name is a general word for the flowering plant.

clue.text: Strengthening rod beginning to bend in tower

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: to tower is to rear up high

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A steel strengthening rod starts to buckle inside a tall tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' reads as a building but is a verb: to rear up. REBAR is the steel bar set in concrete to reinforce it.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for reinforcing bar, it is the ribbed steel rod embedded in concrete to give it tensile strength.

clue.text: Concert one left feeling overwhelmed by cuteness

parts.note: a gig is a live music concert
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A lone fan at a concert, left giddy by how adorable the band is.
explanation.walkthrough: GIGIL is a Filipino loanword for the urge to squeeze or pinch something unbearably cute.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagalog word names the gritted-teeth urge to squeeze something adorable, now listed in English dictionaries as that emotion.

clue.text: Streaming a Welsh female embracing Unilever soap brand

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one word wraps round another

parts.note: Ffion is a Welsh girl's name
Lux is a long-running Unilever toilet soap

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman is caught streaming an advert for a famous Unilever soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaming' looks like modern video, but it is the old sense of flowing. AFFLUXION is an archaic word for a flowing towards a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a flowing to or towards something, so it fits streaming used as a noun for the act of flowing.

clue.text: Chinese city supplants focus of preliminary survey in old people's home

indicators.note: to supplant is to take another's place, so one chunk ousts another

parts.note: a recce is a reconnaissance, a preliminary look round

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its central point, its middle letter

parts.note: the central letter of that five-letter word
Sian is the older spelling of Xi'an

explanation.surface: A Chinese city takes over the central part of a planning survey for a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people's home' suggests a care home, but 'old' marks an archaic word and 'people's home' is the definition. RESIANCE is an obsolete word for residence.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic term meant one's dwelling or abode, so an obsolete word for the place where people live.

clue.text: Atlantic swimmer's medal wrapped in Arabian flag

definitions.note: the clue's 's reads as 'is', so the definition is the swimmer itself, a noun matching the answer

indicators.note: something wrapped in a covering sits inside it

parts.note: Ar. is the abbreviation for Arabian or Arabic
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
a jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow

explanation.surface: A cross-Atlantic swimmer receives her medal draped in an Arabian flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person; it is a fish. The AMBERJACK is a large game fish found in the Atlantic and elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Amberjacks are big predatory fish of warm Atlantic waters, so calling one an Atlantic swimmer describes it by habitat.

clue.text: Blind, lost relatives going back and forth

indicators.note: going forth means moving forwards, so this piece reads in its normal direction
a piece going back reads the other way, right to left

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, a brother or sister
a son is another relative

explanation.surface: Someone blind and lost, with family members pacing back and forth looking for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatives' supplies two kin words, one read backwards and one forwards. 'Lost' adds nothing to the letters. BISSON is a Shakespearean word for blind or purblind.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means sightless or nearly so, used by Shakespeare in Hamlet and Coriolanus, so it is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Censor checks pompous sort before start of inquest on old Venetian spendthrift

indicators.note: a piece placed before another comes first in the reading
to check something is to hold it in, so one word restrains another inside it

parts.note: to censor something is to ban it
a pompous fool is an ass

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A censor reins in a pompous figure ahead of an inquest into an old Venetian wastrel.
explanation.walkthrough: BASSANIO is Antonio's friend in The Merchant of Venice, who has squandered his fortune and borrows to woo Portia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play this Venetian gentleman has 'disabled his estate' through lavish living, which makes him a spendthrift of Venice.

clue.text: Evil cloaked in unlimited panic reflected matter of concern for Mandela?

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round
something cloaked in a garment is wrapped inside it
without its limits, a word loses its outer letters and keeps its middle

parts.note: the inner letters of the word
evil means bad

explanation.surface: Evil hides behind a mask of calm while Mandela weighs an issue of national concern.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal applies to the whole assembly, not just the inner piece. INDABA is a Zulu word for a conference, and in South African English a matter that is one's own concern.
explanation.definitionFit: South Africans say 'that's your indaba' meaning your business or concern, and Mandela, being South African, makes the question mark fair.

clue.text: Skim-read papers, looking up horse

indicators.note: in a down entry, something looking up faces the top, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: papers proving who you are are your ID
a pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse

explanation.surface: Someone skims the newspapers, glancing up for tips on a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' suggests newspapers, but it is identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip into a book is to read bits of it casually, the same light sampling that skim-reading describes.

clue.text: Fragmented Thracian pottery cups

indicators.note: a fragmented thing is broken into pieces that can be put back in another order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Archaeologists dig up shards of Thracian earthenware drinking vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: A CANTHARUS (plural CANTHARI) is an ancient Greek two-handled drinking cup, so the fragmented Thracian pottery is fittingly a pile of them.
explanation.definitionFit: These were deep two-handled drinking vessels of Greek earthenware, associated with Dionysus, so plural cups of fired clay.

clue.text: French theological scholar pounds into a clock accessory

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something put into another goes inside it

parts.note: clock is slang for face, and a beard is a face accessory
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A French theologian hammers something onto a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is British slang for a face, so its accessory is facial hair. ABELARD is Peter Abelard, the twelfth-century philosopher famous for his love affair with Héloïse.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard was a Breton-born scholastic philosopher and theologian of medieval Paris, so he is a French scholar of theology.

clue.text: Alga perished around small (minute) stems

indicators.note: turned around means facing the opposite way, so the word reads backwards
to stem a flow is to plug it, and a plug sits lodged inside the channel

parts.note: to perish is to die
S is the abbreviation for small
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A small piece of algae died, clinging round some tiny plant stems.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets are surface dressing and carry no wordplay. A DESMID is a single-celled freshwater green alga.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmids are microscopic green algae of fresh water, often symmetrical in two halves, so it is one kind of alga.

clue.text: Daredevil for one twice snubbed extremely tendentious receivers

indicators.note: a snub cuts something short, and doing it twice docks two letters from the end

parts.note: Daredevil is a Marvel comics superhero

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A reckless thrill-seeker, twice rebuffed, faces some highly biased listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' marks Daredevil as an example of a class. SUPERHETS is short for superheterodyne radio receivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhet is a radio set using the superheterodyne circuit, so these are radio receivers by type of design.

clue.text: Call interrupted by hospital unit

indicators.note: a word interrupted by something has it break in at the middle

parts.note: to call something by a name is to term it
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A phone call is cut short by a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' looks like a hospital ward but is a unit of measure. A THERM is 100,000 British thermal units, used for gas billing in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a measurement of heat energy used on British gas bills, a specific unit by any definition.

clue.text: Representative melody with finale in part rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, something rising reads from bottom to top
the closing letter is put inside the next word rather than left at the end

parts.note: a lay is a song or melody
pt is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: A representative's tune climbs to a rousing finish in part of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the melody's last letter moves inside the abbreviation; the rest stays in front, and the whole reads upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Typal means typical or serving as a type, so it describes something representative of its kind.

clue.text: Acting family loving Andalusia's first tavern there?

parts.note: to be fond is to be loving

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A family of actors, devoted to the first inn they find in southern Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay sits between two definitions: the Fondas (Henry, Jane, Peter, Bridget) are a Hollywood acting dynasty, and a fonda is a Spanish inn; 'there' points back to Andalusia.
explanation.definitionFit: Fonda is Spanish for an inn or tavern, and the surname names an American acting dynasty, so both readings land on one word.

clue.text: Patronisingly elaborate electricity supply scheme in which current is delayed

indicators.note: something delayed is held back from where it should appear, so it leaves its first place

parts.note: the mains is the domestic electricity supply

indicators.note: a thing in which something sits holds it inside, so a letter is put back within

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A power company lays out a convoluted electricity supply plan in which the current is held up.
explanation.walkthrough: MAINS PLAN would be the obvious phrase, but its current is held back to a later spot. To MANSPLAIN is for a man to explain something condescendingly, usually to a woman who knows it already.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes a man explaining condescendingly at needless length, so to elaborate patronisingly is a fair gloss.

clue.text: Wake-up call aimlessly drew in Aussie lookout taking time off

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, here the letter for time
one thing sitting in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: in Australian slang a cockatoo is a lookout posted during illegal activity
to doodle is to draw aimlessly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An Australian sentry, idly sketching while on watch, misses his wake-up alarm on his day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aimlessly' looks like an anagram signal, but 'aimlessly drew' is a past-tense verb meaning scribbled. The bird word loses its T and the scribble goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the rooster's crow at dawn, traditionally what rouses a farmyard, so it is a call that wakes people up.
